answer: Each agent’s influence can be tied to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is gradually earned through useful work and slashed when independent audits catch fraud. A new identity starts with no reputation, so splitting one stake across many agents does not multiply voting power; each must earn trust separately. The ridge of an audit trail can expose coordinated claims, while a pigment-like mark records who backed them across a terrace of tasks. The attacker must lock up more capital and spend time building credible histories, making mass Sybil identities costly.
